methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
Ephos is a seed-stage semiconductor company founded by Andrea Rocchetto, Francesco Ceccarelli, and Ciro Pentangelo. The company has raised €41.5M from EU sources plus $8.5M in seed funding. The semiconductor sector contains 11 peer companies across public and private markets: 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers, including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable to Ephos. The universe of same-stage semiconductor companies yielded zero qualifying matches; adjacent-stage and similar-valuation-tier filters identified only one datapoint each. A minimum of three comparable transactions is required to establish defensible multiples, and the narrow peer set does not meet this threshold. Applying an all-sector median would introduce material distortion given Ephos's frontier-tech positioning and the heterogeneity of semiconductor subsectors.

The sparsity of seed-stage semiconductor comparables reflects the capital intensity and technical risk of the sector. Without sufficient triangulation data, valuation cannot be reliably derived from peer multiples. Alternative approaches—including discounted cash flow analysis tied to technical milestones, or venture method calibration to stage-specific failure rates—would be necessary to establish a defensible range. Key uncertainties include product commercialization timeline, competitive positioning within the fragmented chip design landscape, and path to revenue sustainability.
